service: SASSA - South African Social Security Agency
overview: SASSA administers social grants to eligible South African citizens, permanent residents, and refugees. It is the primary social safety net for over 28 million grant recipients in South Africa. SASSA operates under the Social Assistance Act 13 of 2004 and is overseen by the Department of Social Development (DSD).

grants.name: Social Relief of Distress (SRD) Grant / R370 Grant
eligibility: South African citizen, permanent resident, or refugee with valid documentation
Between 18 and 60 years old
Unemployed and not receiving any other social grant or UIF
Monthly income below R625 (verified against SARS, UIF, banks, and other government databases)
Not a full-time student at a government-funded institution receiving NSFAS
Not resident in a government-funded institution (prison, state care facility, etc.)
Must not be a registered taxpayer earning above the threshold
Must not have a spouse or partner whose income disqualifies you
how_to_apply: Apply online at srd.sassa.gov.za — this is the ONLY official application channel for SRD
You need your South African ID number (13-digit ID number)
Provide an active cellphone number registered in your name for OTP verification
Provide banking details (FNB, Absa, Standard Bank, Nedbank, Capitec, TymeBank, African Bank, Postbank) or select Post Office cash collection
Complete the SRD online application form — no paper forms are used for this grant
Application is reviewed monthly — you MUST reconfirm by the 25th of each month
If you miss the reconfirmation deadline of the 25th, you will not be considered for that month's payment

how_to_reconfirm: Log into srd.sassa.gov.za and confirm under 'Application Status'
reconfirmation.what_happens_if_missed: You are automatically excluded from that month's payment cycle. You must reconfirm the following month to be reconsidered. There is no back-pay for months you missed reconfirmation.

processing_timeline.income_verification: SASSA cross-checks your details against SARS, banks, UIF, NSFAS, Department of Home Affairs, and company payroll databases
processing_timeline.payment_after_approval: Payment is typically made between the 15th and the last day of the month, but dates vary each cycle
processing_timeline.payment_method_change: Takes effect in the next payment cycle (not the current month)

status_checking.online: Visit srd.sassa.gov.za → click 'SRD Status Check' → enter ID number and phone number
status_checking.ussd: Dial *134*7737# from any cellphone (no airtime needed, it is a free USSD code)
status_checking.whatsapp: Send your ID number to 082 046 8553 on WhatsApp
status_checking.call: Phone 0800 60 10 11 (toll-free from a landline) or 021 469 0111 (from a cellphone, standard rates apply)

common_rejection_reasons: Income above R625 per month detected via bank account checks or SARS records
Receiving another social grant (child support grant income is counted)
UIF payments detected (even a single payment in the assessment period)
SARS database shows employment or tax registration with income
Company payroll databases (IRP5 data) show recent employment
Failed identity verification (ID number mismatch, deceased status on Home Affairs system)
Applicant identified as a director of a registered company (CIPC records)
Bank account shows deposits exceeding the income threshold
Duplicate application detected (same ID number on multiple applications)
appeal_process: You can appeal within 90 days of the rejection decision
Appeal online at srd.sassa.gov.za under the 'Appeal' section — you need your ID number and the phone number linked to your application
Upload or provide supporting documents: affidavit of unemployment, bank statements showing no income, letter of retrenchment, UIF exhaustion letter
Appeals are first reviewed internally by SASSA within 30 days
If the internal appeal is rejected, escalate to the Independent Tribunal for Social Assistance Appeals (ITSAA)
If ITSAA rejects your appeal, you may approach the High Court for judicial review (you will need legal assistance — contact Legal Aid SA at 0800 110 110)

escalation.body: Independent Tribunal for Social Assistance Appeals (ITSAA)
escalation.ombudsman: If SASSA fails to process your appeal within 90 days, you may approach the Public Protector at 0800 11 20 40
escalation.legal_aid: Legal Aid South Africa: 0800 110 110 (free legal representation for qualifying applicants)

grants.name: Child Support Grant (CSG)
eligibility: Primary caregiver of a child under 18 years old
South African citizen, permanent resident, or refugee
Caregiver income must be below R5,600 per month (single) or R11,200 combined (married/cohabiting)
Child must not be in a government-funded institution (children's home, foster care facility)
Both caregiver and child must reside in South Africa
The caregiver does not need to be the biological parent — grandparents, aunts, uncles, or any person primarily caring for the child can apply
No more than 6 children per caregiver (biological parent has no limit for their own biological children)

means_test.single_caregiver_income_limit: R5,600 per month / R67,200 per year
means_test.married_combined_income_limit: R11,200 per month / R134,400 per year
what_counts_as_income: Informal employment income (piece jobs, self-employment, hawking)
Other social grants received (except the CSG being applied for)
what_does_not_count_as_income: Gifts and donations under R1,000 per month
Food parcels or donations in kind
means_test.assets_not_tested: The Child Support Grant does not have an asset/property test — only income is assessed

required_documents: Caregiver's ID document (original or certified copy, not older than 3 months)
Child's birth certificate (unabridged birth certificate preferred)
Proof of income: latest payslip, or a sworn affidavit confirming unemployment (can be done free at a police station or commissioner of oaths)
Proof of residence: utility bill, letter from traditional authority, or affidavit
If the child's surname differs from the caregiver's: a sworn affidavit explaining the caregiving arrangement
If married: spouse's ID and proof of spouse's income
3 months' bank statements (if you have a bank account)
required_forms: SASSA Social Grant Application Form (available at any SASSA office, free of charge)
Sworn affidavit of unemployment (if unemployed — free at South African Police Service or commissioner of oaths)
Caregiver affidavit (if the applicant is not the biological parent)
how_to_apply: Visit your nearest SASSA office in person — no appointment is needed but arrive early as queues can be very long
Collect and complete the SASSA application form at the office (free of charge)
Submit your ID, child's birth certificate, proof of income (payslip or unemployment affidavit), and proof of residence
SASSA will verify your information against government databases
SASSA must process the application within 30 days by law (Regulation 10(2))
You will receive an SMS notification of the outcome
If approved, back-pay is paid from the date of application (not the date of approval)

processing_timeline.first_payment_after_approval: Within 30-60 days of approval, depending on pay cycle
processing_timeline.back_pay: You are entitled to back-pay from the date you submitted your application

grants.payment_dates: 7th to 9th of each month (children's grants are paid in this window)
common_problems: Grant suspended without notification — usually due to child turning 18, income change detected, or child registered as deceased on Home Affairs system
Payment not received on expected date — check with SASSA (0800 60 10 11) or your bank; payment delays of 1-3 days are common at month-end
Someone else claiming the grant for your child — report fraud to SASSA fraud hotline 0800 701 701
Grant lapses if not collected for 3 consecutive months — must reapply
Banking details changed by someone else — report immediately to SASSA and request a freeze on changes
Deductions from grant by loan sharks or microfinance — this is illegal under Regulation 26 of the Social Assistance Act; report to SASSA

escalation.timeframe: SASSA must process applications within 30 days per Regulation 10(2)
escalation.appeal_body: Independent Tribunal for Social Assistance Appeals (ITSAA) — 012 312 7466

grants.name: Older Persons Grant (Old Age Pension)
grants.amount: R2,180 per month (aged 60-74) / R2,200 per month (aged 75 and older) (2024/2025)
eligibility: South African citizen, permanent resident, or refugee
60 years or older (both men and women — the age was equalised)
Income below R7,710 per month (single) or R15,420 combined (married/cohabiting)
Assets below R1,372,800 (single) or R2,745,600 (married/cohabiting)
Not maintained in a state institution (old age home funded by government)
Not receiving any other social grant (except Grant-in-Aid, which can be added on top)

means_test.single_income_limit: R7,710 per month / R92,520 per year
means_test.married_income_limit: R15,420 per month combined / R185,040 per year combined
what_counts_as_assets: Property (excluding the home you live in — your primary residence is excluded)
Savings and investments (bank accounts, unit trusts, shares, stokvels over certain thresholds)
Life insurance policies with cash/surrender value
Any other assets with monetary value
what_does_not_count_as_assets: Your primary residence (the house you live in)
One vehicle used for personal transport (some discretion applies)

required_documents: South African ID document (original or certified copy not older than 3 months)
Proof of residence (utility bill, municipal account, or affidavit)
3 months' bank statements for all bank accounts
Proof of income (pension payslips, rental income proof, investment statements)
If married: spouse's ID, income proof, and bank statements
If you own property: municipal valuation or title deed
Proof of any insurance policies or investments
required_forms: SASSA Social Grant Application Form (free at any SASSA office)
Means test declaration form (completed at the office)
how_to_apply: Visit your nearest SASSA office in person
Bring your ID, proof of residence, bank statements (3 months for all accounts), and proof of any income or assets
If married, bring spouse's ID, income proof, and bank statements
Complete the SASSA application form and means test declaration at the office
Processing takes up to 30 days (legally mandated)
If approved, you receive back-pay from the date of application

processing_timeline.back_pay: Paid from date of application, not date of approval
processing_timeline.medical_review_for_frail_aged: Not required — the Older Persons Grant is age-based, not medically assessed

grants.payment_dates: 1st to 3rd of each month (older persons are paid first in the payment cycle)
common_problems: Grant reduced because spouse's income or pension pushes combined income higher
Grant suspended because SASSA detected income from an investment or property rental
Grant stopped after moving to a state-funded institution — you must notify SASSA of any change in living arrangements
Deductions from SASSA gold card by unauthorised third parties — report immediately to SASSA

escalation.legislation: Social Assistance Act 13 of 2004, Older Persons Act 13 of 2006

grants.name: Disability Grant

types.temporary: Granted for 6 to 12 months — must be reassessed before expiry to continue receiving the grant
types.permanent: Granted when the disability is confirmed as permanent by the SASSA-appointed medical officer — no expiry but subject to periodic review

eligibility: South African citizen, permanent resident, or refugee
Between 18 and 59 years old (at age 60 you automatically transition to Older Persons Grant)
Must have a disability that prevents you from entering the open labour market
Must be assessed and confirmed by a SASSA-appointed medical officer (you cannot use your own doctor's letter alone)
Income below R7,710 per month (single) or R15,420 combined (married/cohabiting)
Assets below R1,372,800 (single) or R2,745,600 (married/cohabiting)
Not maintained in a state institution

means_test.single_income_limit: R7,710 per month / R92,520 per year
means_test.married_income_limit: R15,420 per month combined / R185,040 per year combined

required_documents: South African ID document (original or certified copy not older than 3 months)
Medical records: hospital discharge summaries, specialist reports, chronic medication scripts, X-rays or scan reports
Proof of residence
3 months' bank statements
Proof of income (if any) or sworn affidavit of unemployment
If married: spouse's ID, income proof, and bank statements
required_forms: SASSA Social Grant Application Form (free at SASSA office)
SASSA Medical/Disability Assessment Form (completed by SASSA-appointed doctor — not your private doctor)
how_to_apply: Visit your nearest SASSA office in person
Complete the SASSA application form and submit your documents
SASSA will book a medical assessment appointment for you — this is FREE; do not pay anyone
Attend the medical assessment on the booked date (if you miss it, you must rebook and the process starts again)
Bring all medical records, hospital letters, and chronic medication scripts to the assessment
The SASSA-appointed medical officer will determine if you qualify and whether the disability is temporary (6-12 months) or permanent
Processing takes up to 30 days from the date of medical assessment (not from application date)

processing_timeline.application_to_medical_assessment: 7-30 days depending on availability at your local SASSA office
processing_timeline.total_process: Can take 30-90 days from initial application to first payment
processing_timeline.temporary_grant_renewal: Apply for renewal at least 90 days before expiry date to avoid a gap in payments
processing_timeline.transition_to_old_age: At age 60, your disability grant automatically converts to the Older Persons Grant — no action needed

common_problems: Temporary disability grant expiring — reapply at least 90 days before the expiry date shown on your approval letter
Medical assessment outcome disputed — request a review or second assessment in writing at your SASSA office
Grant stopped unexpectedly — contact SASSA immediately with your reference number; common causes are missed review dates or data errors
Approved for temporary when you believe your condition is permanent — appeal the decision and provide additional specialist medical evidence
Medical assessment booking delays — if SASSA takes longer than 30 days to book your assessment, lodge a complaint at the office and escalate to SASSA head office

escalation.medical_dispute: You may request a second medical assessment. If still disputed, escalate to ITSAA with supporting medical evidence from your treating specialist.

grants.name: Foster Child Grant
eligibility: You must have a valid foster care court order issued by the Children's Court (Form 30 order)
The child must be under 18 years old
You must be a South African citizen, permanent resident, or refugee
No means test is applied — the Foster Child Grant is not income-tested
The court order must be current and valid (not expired)

court_order_requirements.initial_order: Issued by the Children's Court after a social worker investigation and report
court_order_requirements.renewal: The foster care court order must be renewed every 2 years — if it expires, the grant is automatically suspended
court_order_requirements.renewal_process: The designated social worker must file an extension report with the Children's Court before the order expires. Contact your social worker at least 3-4 months before expiry to start the process.
court_order_requirements.lapsed_orders: If the court order lapses, you must apply for a new court order through the Children's Court. During this period, no grant is payable. Back-pay may be possible if the delay was caused by the Department of Social Development (DSD), not the foster parent.
court_order_requirements.crisis: There is a national backlog in foster care order renewals. If your social worker is unresponsive, contact the DSD provincial office directly or approach the Centre for Child Law at the University of Pretoria (012 420 4502) for assistance.

required_documents: Valid foster care court order (Form 30 — original or certified copy)
Foster parent's ID document (original or certified copy not older than 3 months)
Child's birth certificate (unabridged preferred)
Social worker's report (SASSA obtains this from DSD — you do not need to bring it)
Proof of residence
required_forms: SASSA Social Grant Application Form (free at SASSA office)
Certified copy of Children's Court order (Form 30)
how_to_apply: First, contact a social worker at the Department of Social Development to initiate the foster care process (this can take several months)
The social worker investigates and submits a report to the Children's Court
The Children's Court issues a foster care court order (Form 30)
Take the court order to your nearest SASSA office with your ID and child's birth certificate
SASSA processes the grant within 30 days
Back-pay is paid from the date the court order was issued (not the date you visited SASSA)

processing_timeline.social_worker_investigation: 2-6 months (this is the longest part of the process due to backlogs)
processing_timeline.court_order_issuance: 1-3 months after social worker report is filed
processing_timeline.sassa_processing: Up to 30 days after submitting at SASSA office
processing_timeline.court_order_renewal: Start the process 3-4 months before the 2-year expiry

grants.payment_dates: 7th to 9th of each month (same window as Child Support Grant)
common_problems: Court order expired and grant was suspended — contact your social worker immediately to file for renewal
Social worker is unresponsive — escalate to the DSD district office or provincial office
Child turning 18 — the grant ends the month the child turns 18; no extension is possible
Foster parent passed away — another family member can apply for a new court order to continue foster care
Grant lapsed due to non-collection — must reapply if not collected for 3 consecutive months

escalation.legislation: Children's Act 38 of 2005, Social Assistance Act 13 of 2004
escalation.legal_help: Centre for Child Law (University of Pretoria): 012 420 4502; Legal Aid SA: 0800 110 110

grants.name: Care Dependency Grant
eligibility: Parent or primary caregiver of a child under 18 with a severe disability or chronic illness requiring permanent home care
South African citizen, permanent resident, or refugee
Income below R5,600 per month (single caregiver) or R11,200 combined (married/cohabiting)
Assets below R1,372,800 (single) or R2,745,600 (married/cohabiting)
The child must NOT be permanently cared for in a state institution (24-hour care facility funded by government)
The child must be assessed by a SASSA-appointed medical officer who confirms the level of care dependency

means_test.single_income_limit: R5,600 per month / R67,200 per year
means_test.married_income_limit: R11,200 per month combined / R134,400 per year combined

medical_assessment.who_assesses: A SASSA-appointed medical doctor — you CANNOT use a report from your private doctor as the sole basis (but bring your private doctor's reports as supporting evidence)
medical_assessment.what_is_assessed: The child's level of care dependency: whether they require permanent home care due to severe physical, intellectual, or mental disability
conditions_that_typically_qualify: Severe autism spectrum disorder requiring constant supervision
Severe physical disability requiring daily assistance (wheelchair-bound, unable to self-care)
Chronic illnesses requiring permanent home care (severe epilepsy, severe HIV/AIDS-related illness in children)
Down syndrome with significant developmental delays
Severe visual or hearing impairment in combination with other disabilities
medical_assessment.reassessment: SASSA may require periodic medical reassessment, especially for conditions that may improve. You will be notified by SMS or letter.

required_documents: Caregiver's ID document (original or certified copy not older than 3 months)
Child's birth certificate (unabridged preferred)
Medical records: specialist reports, hospital records, therapy reports, chronic medication scripts
Proof of income or sworn affidavit of unemployment
Proof of residence
3 months' bank statements
If married: spouse's ID, income proof, and bank statements
School attendance records or letter from special school (if applicable)
required_forms: SASSA Social Grant Application Form (free at SASSA office)
SASSA Medical/Care Dependency Assessment Form (completed by SASSA-appointed doctor)
how_to_apply: Visit your nearest SASSA office with all documents
Complete the application form and submit documents
SASSA will book a medical assessment for the child — this is FREE
Attend the medical assessment with the child and bring ALL medical records and specialist reports
Processing takes up to 30 days from the medical assessment date
grants.payment_dates: 7th to 9th of each month (children's grants payment window)
grants.transition_at_18: When the child turns 18, the Care Dependency Grant ends. The now-adult child can apply for a Disability Grant in their own name if they still have a qualifying disability.

escalation.medical_dispute: If you disagree with the medical assessment outcome, request a review in writing and provide additional specialist reports.

grants.name: Grant-in-Aid
grants.amount: R530 per month (2024/2025) — paid IN ADDITION to your existing grant
eligibility: Already receiving an Older Persons Grant, Disability Grant, or War Veterans Grant
Require regular attendance/care by another person due to physical or mental condition
The person caring for you does not need to be a professional caregiver — a family member or community member qualifies
Must be assessed by SASSA (may require medical assessment)
how_to_apply: Visit your nearest SASSA office with your ID and proof of your existing grant
A SASSA official or medical officer will assess your care needs
No separate means test — you already qualified for the underlying grant
grants.payment_dates: Paid on the same date as your primary grant (1st-3rd for older persons, 4th-6th for disability)

grants.name: War Veterans Grant
eligibility: South African citizen who served in the Second World War, Korean War, or the South African liberation struggle
60 years or older, or disabled as a result of service
Income below R7,710 per month (single) or R15,420 combined (married)
Assets below R1,372,800 (single) or R2,745,600 (married)
how_to_apply: Visit your nearest SASSA office with your ID, proof of military service, proof of income and assets
Processing takes up to 30 days

payment_schedule.srd_grant: Varies — typically between the 15th and last day of the month; exact dates announced by SASSA each cycle
payment_schedule.note: If the payment date falls on a weekend or public holiday, payment is made on the last business day before that date. SASSA publishes the exact payment schedule on www.sassa.gov.za at the beginning of each financial year.

sassa_gold_card.description: SASSA-issued Postbank debit card (gold card) linked to your SASSA account
sassa_gold_card.where_to_use: Any ATM (Saswitch network), Post Office, retail merchants (Shoprite, Pick n Pay, Boxer, Usave, Checkers, SPAR), and SASSA pay points
sassa_gold_card.fees: One free cash withdrawal per month at the Post Office or SASSA pay point. ATM withdrawals may incur bank fees. Point-of-sale purchases at retailers are generally free.
sassa_gold_card.problems: If your card is lost/stolen, report immediately to SASSA (0800 60 10 11) or Postbank (0800 53 54 55). A replacement card takes 5-14 days.

bank_account.description: Grant paid directly into your bank account at any South African bank
bank_account.accepted_banks: FNB, Absa, Standard Bank, Nedbank, Capitec, TymeBank, African Bank, Postbank, Discovery Bank, and other registered SA banks
bank_account.requirements: Bank account must be in the grant recipient's name. Joint accounts are not accepted for individual grants.
bank_account.changing_bank_details: Visit a SASSA office with your ID and new bank card/proof of account. Changes take effect in the next payment cycle. Do NOT give your banking details to anyone who phones or messages you claiming to be from SASSA.

post_office_cash.description: Collect cash at any South African Post Office branch
post_office_cash.requirements: Bring your SASSA gold card and ID or your green bar-coded ID book
post_office_cash.hours: Post Office hours: Monday to Friday 08:00-16:30, some branches open Saturday 08:00-12:00

retail_cash_withdrawal.description: Cash back or withdrawal at participating retailers
retail_cash_withdrawal.retailers: Shoprite, Checkers, Pick n Pay, Boxer, Usave, SPAR (select branches)
retail_cash_withdrawal.limit: Subject to the retailer's cash-back limits, typically R500-R2,000 per transaction
retail_cash_withdrawal.note: You can also use your SASSA gold card to pay for groceries directly at the till — no need to withdraw cash first

all_grants_except_srd.phone: Call SASSA toll-free at 0800 60 10 11 (Monday to Friday 07:30-16:00)
all_grants_except_srd.in_person: Visit your nearest SASSA office with your ID — a consultant will check your status on the system
all_grants_except_srd.email: Send your enquiry to grantenquiries@sassa.gov.za with your ID number and reference number

srd_grant_specific.website: Visit srd.sassa.gov.za → click 'SRD Status Check' → enter your ID number and phone number linked to your application
srd_grant_specific.ussd: Dial *134*7737# from any cellphone (free — no airtime required) → follow the prompts to check status
srd_grant_specific.whatsapp: Send your ID number to 082 046 8553 on WhatsApp → the automated system will reply with your status

status_meanings.approved: Your application was successful — payment will be processed according to the payment schedule
status_meanings.pending: Your application is still being processed — SASSA is verifying your information
status_meanings.declined: Your application was rejected — check the reason given and appeal if you believe it is incorrect
status_meanings.reconfirmation_needed: SRD only: you must reconfirm by the 25th of the month to continue receiving the grant
status_meanings.referred: Your application has been referred for additional verification or investigation

how_sassa_verifies_income: SARS (South African Revenue Service) employment records and tax returns
UIF (Unemployment Insurance Fund) records — checks if you are receiving or have recently received UIF payments
NSFAS (National Student Financial Aid Scheme) records — checks if you receive student funding
Bank account records — SASSA can request transaction histories from any bank
CIPC (Companies and Intellectual Property Commission) — checks if you are a registered company director
Department of Labour payroll data (IRP5 submissions by employers)
Other government grant databases — checks if you are receiving any other grant
Cross-referencing with Department of Home Affairs for identity and marital status verification
what_counts_as_income: Formal employment: salary, wages, commission, overtime, bonuses
Informal employment: income from piece jobs, domestic work, gardening, hawking, street vending, and other informal work
Self-employment: business income, freelance work, online work
Other social grants: the amount of other grants you receive counts as income when applying for additional grants
Maintenance payments: child maintenance or spousal maintenance received
UIF/TERS payments: unemployment or temporary employer relief payments
Rental income: income from renting out property or rooms
Pension/retirement income: private pension, provident fund, retirement annuity payments
Investment income: dividends, interest, returns from unit trusts or shares
Bursaries and stipends: if they provide a living allowance (but study-only bursaries are treated differently)
what_does_not_count_as_income: Gifts and donations under R1,000 per month (casual gifts from family or community)
Once-off insurance claim payouts (car accident, household insurance)
Food parcels and donations in kind (food hampers, clothing donations from NGOs)
Disability equipment grants from the Department of Health
Compensation for occupational injuries (COIDA) in some circumstances — treated case-by-case
common_disputes: SASSA detected income that no longer exists (e.g., you were retrenched but your IRP5 still shows last year's employment) — provide a retrenchment letter and UIF exhaustion letter
Income from informal work fluctuates month to month — provide an affidavit explaining the irregular nature of your income
SASSA counted a once-off deposit as monthly income — provide proof that it was a gift, insurance payout, or other excluded income type
Spouse or partner's income counted incorrectly — provide their actual payslip and bank statements to show the correct amount

appeal_process.overview: If your grant application is rejected or your existing grant is suspended or cancelled, you have the right to appeal. The appeal process has three levels.

step_1_sassa_internal_appeal.description: First lodge an appeal with SASSA itself
step_1_sassa_internal_appeal.deadline: Within 90 days of the rejection or adverse decision
how_to_appeal: For SRD grant: Appeal online at srd.sassa.gov.za under the 'Appeal' section
For all other grants: Visit your nearest SASSA office and complete the DSD/SASSA appeal form
Submit supporting documents: affidavit, bank statements, medical records, retrenchment letter — anything that supports your case
Keep a copy of everything you submit and get a receipt/reference number from SASSA
step_1_sassa_internal_appeal.processing_time: SASSA should process internal appeals within 30 days, but in practice it can take 30-90 days
step_1_sassa_internal_appeal.required_form: DSD/SASSA Appeal Form (available free at any SASSA office)

step_2_itsaa.description: If SASSA rejects your internal appeal (or fails to respond within 90 days), escalate to the Independent Tribunal for Social Assistance Appeals (ITSAA)
step_2_itsaa.what_is_itsaa: An independent body established under Section 18 of the Social Assistance Act to hear appeals against SASSA decisions
how_to_appeal: Write a letter or complete the ITSAA appeal form, explaining why you believe the decision was wrong
Attach copies of your original application, the rejection letter, your SASSA internal appeal documents, and any supporting evidence
Send by registered post to ITSAA at 368 Madiba Street, Pretoria Central, 0001, or hand-deliver
You can also email your appeal to appeals@socdev.gov.za
step_2_itsaa.processing_time: ITSAA hearings can take 30-90 days. You may be called to attend a hearing in person or telephonically.
step_2_itsaa.cost: Free — there is no charge for an ITSAA appeal

step_3_high_court_review.description: If ITSAA rejects your appeal, or if you believe the process was unfair or unlawful, you can approach the High Court for a judicial review
step_3_high_court_review.basis: Promotion of Administrative Justice Act (PAJA) — judicial review of administrative action
step_3_high_court_review.deadline: Within 180 days of the ITSAA decision
step_3_high_court_review.cost: Court proceedings are expensive — apply for free legal assistance through Legal Aid SA (0800 110 110) or approach the Black Sash (021 686 6952) or a university law clinic
step_3_high_court_review.note: High Court review is a last resort. Most cases are resolved at the SASSA internal appeal or ITSAA level.

organisations_that_can_help_with_appeals.name: Legal Aid South Africa
organisations_that_can_help_with_appeals.service: Free legal representation for qualifying individuals (means-tested)

organisations_that_can_help_with_appeals.name: Black Sash
organisations_that_can_help_with_appeals.service: Community-based advice on social grants, assistance with appeals, monitoring SASSA services

organisations_that_can_help_with_appeals.name: South African Human Rights Commission (SAHRC)
organisations_that_can_help_with_appeals.service: Investigates complaints about violations of the right to social security

organisations_that_can_help_with_appeals.name: Public Protector
organisations_that_can_help_with_appeals.service: Investigates maladministration — e.g., SASSA failing to process your application or appeal within the required timeframe

organisations_that_can_help_with_appeals.name: Centre for Child Law (University of Pretoria)
organisations_that_can_help_with_appeals.service: Specialist help with children's grants, foster care, and care dependency issues

immediate_steps: Check your grant status by calling 0800 60 10 11 or visiting srd.sassa.gov.za (for SRD)
Check that your banking details have not been changed — if they were changed without your consent, report fraud immediately
Visit your nearest SASSA office with your ID and proof of banking details within 90 days of the missed payment
Ask SASSA for the specific reason the payment was stopped — they are legally required to tell you
common_causes: Banking details were changed (by you or fraudulently by someone else)
Your bank account was closed by the bank
Income or employment was detected in a government database
Your grant period expired (temporary disability, foster care court order expired)
You did not collect your grant for 3 consecutive months (grant lapses automatically)
The beneficiary (child, older person) passed away and Home Affairs updated their records
SRD: You did not reconfirm by the 25th of the month
System error at SASSA — these are more common than SASSA admits; insist on a printout of your file
back_pay_rules: If the payment stoppage was SASSA's fault (system error, administrative delay), you are entitled to back-pay for all missed months
If you failed to collect for 3 months and the grant lapsed, you must reapply — back-pay is only from the new application date
If your grant was wrongly suspended and you appeal successfully, you are entitled to back-pay for the full suspension period
SASSA cannot refuse back-pay if the delay was on their side — this is established by multiple court rulings
what_to_do_if_payment_stops.deadline: Report a missed payment to SASSA within 90 days. After 90 days, it becomes much harder to recover the payment.

lapsed_grants.what_happens: If you do not collect your grant for 3 consecutive months, the grant is automatically suspended (lapsed). SASSA assumes you no longer need the grant or are no longer eligible.
consequences: The grant is suspended and you stop receiving payments
You must visit a SASSA office to reactivate or reapply
For SRD, you must submit a new application online
Back-pay for the lapsed months is generally NOT paid — you only receive payments going forward from the reactivation/reapplication date
If the lapse was due to circumstances beyond your control (hospitalisation, imprisonment, etc.), bring proof and request back-pay — SASSA may consider it on a case-by-case basis
how_to_reactivate: Visit your nearest SASSA office with your ID and existing grant reference number
SASSA will verify your continued eligibility
If you still qualify, the grant may be reactivated without a full new application (for older persons, disability, and child support grants)
For foster child grants, your court order must still be valid
For SRD, you must submit a completely new online application
lapsed_grants.prevention: If you know you will be unable to collect your grant (hospitalisation, travel, etc.), ask a trusted person with a power of attorney to collect on your behalf, or switch to bank account payment before you leave

common_scams_and_fraud.warning: SASSA will NEVER ask you to pay money for any service. All SASSA applications, assessments, and services are FREE. Anyone who asks you for money is a scammer.

known_scams.type: Fake SASSA agents at pay points
known_scams.description: People wearing fake SASSA-branded clothing approach grant recipients at pay points, Post Offices, or shopping centres and offer to 'help' with applications or card problems. They steal banking details, PINs, or charge fees.
known_scams.how_to_protect_yourself: Never give your SASSA card, PIN, ID, or banking details to anyone outside a SASSA office. Real SASSA officials work INSIDE the office, not outside.

known_scams.description: You receive an SMS saying your grant has been approved or suspended and you must click a link or call a number to 'verify' your details. The link leads to a fake website that steals your information.
known_scams.how_to_protect_yourself: SASSA sends SMS notifications but NEVER asks you to click a link or provide your PIN via SMS. Ignore and delete suspicious messages. Report them to SASSA fraud hotline 0800 701 701.

known_scams.description: Fake WhatsApp accounts pretending to be SASSA ask for your ID number, banking details, or PIN. Some promise to 'fast-track' your application.
known_scams.how_to_protect_yourself: The ONLY official SASSA WhatsApp number is 082 046 8553. It is an automated system that NEVER asks for your PIN or banking details. Block and report any other number.

known_scams.type: Loan deductions / illegal deductions from grants
known_scams.description: Micro-lenders and loan sharks (mashonisas) deduct repayments directly from your SASSA grant or take your SASSA card. Some grant recipients are pressured into taking loans with their grant card as security.
known_scams.how_to_protect_yourself: It is ILLEGAL for any lender to deduct from your SASSA grant or hold your SASSA card. Report any deductions to SASSA (0800 60 10 11) and the National Credit Regulator (0860 627 627). Under Regulation 26 of the Social Assistance Act, social grants are protected from attachment or deductions.

known_scams.description: Someone at or near a SASSA office offers to 'fast-track' or 'speed up' your application for a fee (often R200-R500). Some claim to be SASSA employees or have 'connections inside.'
known_scams.how_to_protect_yourself: No one can fast-track a SASSA application. Applications are processed in order. Report anyone charging fees to the SASSA fraud hotline 0800 701 701 or South African Police Service.

known_scams.description: Fraudulent websites that look like srd.sassa.gov.za but have slightly different URLs (e.g., srd-sassa.co.za, sassagrant.com) collect your personal information.
known_scams.how_to_protect_yourself: The ONLY official SASSA website for SRD applications is srd.sassa.gov.za. The main SASSA website is www.sassa.gov.za. Check the URL carefully before entering any information.

known_scams.description: Someone uses your ID number to apply for a grant in your name, redirecting payments to their bank account.
known_scams.how_to_protect_yourself: If you discover that a grant has been applied for in your name without your consent, report it immediately to SASSA fraud hotline 0800 701 701 and lay a charge at the nearest police station.

where_to_report_fraud.south_african_police_service: Visit your nearest police station and open a fraud case

your_rights: Section 27(1)(c) of the Constitution of South Africa guarantees the right to social security, including the right to appropriate social assistance for those unable to support themselves
SASSA must process applications within 30 days (Regulation 10(2) of the Social Assistance Act) — if they fail to do so, you can lodge a complaint with the Public Protector
You have the right to appeal any decision within 90 days — first to SASSA internally, then to ITSAA, then to the High Court
SASSA must give you written reasons for any rejection — if they refuse, insist and reference Section 5 of the Promotion of Administrative Justice Act (PAJA)
You may NOT be asked to pay any fees for a SASSA application, medical assessment, or any other service — it is ALWAYS free
If SASSA fails to pay your grant on time through their fault, they must provide back-pay for all missed months — this has been confirmed by multiple court orders
You have the right to receive your grant at a pay point or through a payment method of your choice
Your social grant is protected from attachment, garnishee orders, or deductions by creditors or loan companies under Regulation 26 of the Social Assistance Act
No one may take your SASSA card or force you to hand over your PIN — this is a criminal offence
You have the right to be treated with dignity at SASSA offices — report any mistreatment, corruption, or bribery to the SASSA fraud hotline 0800 701 701
If you are a person with a disability, SASSA must make reasonable accommodation for you at their offices (wheelchair access, sign language, priority queuing)
SASSA must provide services in your preferred official language where reasonably possible

frequently_asked_questions.question: Can I receive more than one grant?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: Generally, you can only receive one social grant for yourself. However, a caregiver can receive a Child Support Grant for each qualifying child (up to 6 non-biological children) while also receiving a grant for themselves (e.g., Disability Grant + Child Support Grant for their children). You cannot receive both a Disability Grant and an Older Persons Grant. The Grant-in-Aid is paid on top of your existing Older Persons, Disability, or War Veterans grant.

frequently_asked_questions.question: My child turns 18 — what happens to the Child Support Grant?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: The Child Support Grant automatically stops the month the child turns 18. There is no extension. If the child is still in school (up to Grade 12 / matric), they do not qualify for SRD if they are at a government-funded school. After turning 18 and leaving school, they can apply for the SRD grant if they are unemployed and meet all other criteria.

frequently_asked_questions.question: I was approved for SRD but payment says 'pending' for weeks — what do I do?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: This is common and usually means SASSA is processing payments in batches. Check your status weekly via srd.sassa.gov.za or *134*7737#. If 'pending' persists for more than one full payment cycle, call 0800 60 10 11 or visit your nearest SASSA office. Payment processing can take up to 10 business days after the status changes to 'approved'.

frequently_asked_questions.question: Someone changed my banking details without my permission — what do I do?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: Go to your nearest SASSA office IMMEDIATELY with your ID. Request a freeze on all changes. File a fraud report at SASSA (0800 701 701) and at your nearest police station. SASSA will investigate and reverse the unauthorised change. The process takes 5-14 days. You may miss one payment cycle during the investigation — request back-pay for any missed payment.

frequently_asked_questions.question: I am an asylum seeker — can I get a grant?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: Only recognised refugees with a Section 24 permit (refugee status) qualify for social grants. Asylum seekers with a Section 22 permit (temporary asylum) do NOT qualify for SASSA grants. However, asylum seekers may be eligible for humanitarian assistance through the Department of Social Development or NGOs such as the UNHCR, Scalabrini Centre, or Lawyers for Human Rights.

frequently_asked_questions.question: I live in a rural area with no SASSA office nearby — how do I apply?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: SASSA conducts outreach visits (mobile offices) to rural and remote areas on a scheduled basis. Contact 0800 60 10 11 to find out the next outreach date for your area. For SRD, apply online at srd.sassa.gov.za — you do not need to visit an office. For other grants, ask if your local councillor or community leader can arrange a SASSA outreach visit.
